review_notes: I read the whole file. It has almost no simp attributes. Its own `simp` calls are small and local, with no visible loops or competing rules. The only simp-interface problems I found are missing unfolding lemmas for the non-reducible `def`s `placeMeasure` and `archMeasure`. Downstream code works around them with `unfold` and `split`. I judged that the many other small identities in the file, such as the `volume_image_mul_*` lemmas, should not be simp lemmas. I did not run Lean, so I did not observe any simp behaviour. The proposed lemmas would be of the form `dif_pos`/`dif_neg` and `Measure.pi_pi`, which I expect to be easy but have not compiled.

findings.problem: `placeMeasure` is defined by a `dite` on `w.IsReal`, but the file has no unfolding lemmas for the two cases. Two downstream proofs repeat `unfold placeMeasure; split; next hw => ...` and then re-derive `w.mult = 1` or `w.mult = 2` with local `simp [mult, hw]`. A user who has `hw : w.IsReal` cannot rewrite `placeMeasure F w` to `placeMeasureReal hw` with `simp`/`rw`. The alternative is `unfold`, which exposes the raw `dite` and its `not_isReal_iff_isComplex` proof term.
findings.proposed_change: Add case lemmas right after the definition, with the real case marked `@[simp]`. The first is `placeMeasure_of_isReal (hw : w.IsReal) : placeMeasure F w = placeMeasureReal hw`, proved by `dif_pos hw`. The second is `placeMeasure_of_isComplex (hw : w.IsComplex) : placeMeasure F w = placeMeasureComplex hw`, proved by `dif_neg` plus `not_isReal_iff_isComplex`. Both are hypothesis-guarded and cannot loop, because the right-hand side is a different head constant. Then rewrite `placeMeasure_image_mul` and `isAddHaarMeasure_placeMeasure` with `rcases w.isReal_or_isComplex` and `rw`/`simp [placeMeasure_of_isReal hw]` instead of `unfold` and `split`. If `placeMeasure_of_isComplex` is also made simp, its side goal `hw : w.IsComplex` must be dischargeable. It is not in general, so keep that case non-simp or accept that it only fires with `hw` in context.
findings.benefit: The `dite` is hidden behind a stable interface. The proofs no longer depend on `unfold`/`split` and the exact shape of the `dite`. Later files get a canonical way to reduce the place measure once the place type is known.

evidence.excerpt:
if hw : w.IsReal then placeMeasureReal hw
  else placeMeasureComplex (not_isReal_iff_isComplex.mp hw)

findings.problem: `archMeasure F` is a plain `def` (`Measure.pi (fun w => placeMeasure F w)`) with no simp or rewrite lemma for its values on box sets. The file repeats `unfold archMeasure; rw [Measure.pi_pi]` in several proofs: `isAddLeftInvariant_archMeasure`, `archMeasure_image_mul_pi`, `adelicMeasure_refSet_ne_top` and `adelicMeasure_refSet_ne_zero`. Several of them also need `show archMeasure F _ ≠ ⊤` first, to expose the term. `infMeasure` is a second layer over `archMeasure` and `adelicMeasure` a third layer over `infMeasure`. The `hcompute` step in the main theorem likewise has to go through `Measure.prod_prod`, `unfold refSet` and `harch` by hand.
findings.proposed_change: State the box lemma once: `archMeasure_pi (B : ∀ w, Set w.Completion) : archMeasure F (Set.pi Set.univ B) = ∏ w, placeMeasure F w (B w)`, proved by `unfold archMeasure; exact Measure.pi_pi _ _`, and mark it `@[simp]`. Its left-hand side has the specific head `archMeasure F (Set.pi univ _)`, so it cannot cycle with `Measure.pi_pi`. A companion `adelicMeasure_prod (A B)` would do the same for `adelicMeasure`. Use these in `adelicMeasure_refSet_ne_top` and `adelicMeasure_refSet_ne_zero`, and in the other users listed above. The `unfold`/`show` scaffolding then goes away.
findings.benefit: There is one canonical normal form, a product of place measures, instead of the same `unfold`+`rw [Measure.pi_pi]` repeated by hand. The `ne_top` and `ne_zero` proofs become `simp`-style one-liners.

evidence.excerpt:
· show archMeasure F _ ≠ 0
    unfold archMeasure
    rw [Measure.pi_pi]
